title: Argonaute 2 drives resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors in immunorefractory non-small cell lung cancer
experiments_summary: The study employed two syngeneic murine NSCLC models (LLC and KP cells) with CRISPR-Cas9-mediated Ago2 knockout (ΔAgo2) generated via lentiviral transduction. Subcutaneous tumor implantation in immunocompetent C57BL/6J and Rag2−/− mice assessed the role of adaptive immunity in tumor growth control. Ago2 complementation experiments restored expression in ΔAgo2 cells to confirm phenotype specificity. Pharmacological inhibition of Ago2 was tested using acriflavine (ACF), aurintricarboxylic acid (ATA), and BCI-137, with toxicity evaluated via daily intraperitoneal injections and weight monitoring; non-toxic doses were selected for subsequent in vivo studies. A dsRNA-driven fluorescent reporter system validated RNAi inhibition by ACF and ATA. Anti-PD1 antibody treatment (200 µg, three times weekly) was administered to tumor-bearing mice to evaluate ICI responsiveness, and tumor rechallenge experiments 100 days post-clearance tested immune memory. An orthotopic lung cancer model was established via tail-vein injection of KP cells, with tumor burden quantified by hematoxylin and eosin staining at 3 and 5 weeks. Bulk RNA sequencing (Illumina NovaSeq, aligned to mm10) was performed on whole tumors and cultured LLC cells (wild-type vs. ΔAgo2), with differential expression analyzed by DESeq2 and pathway enrichment via fastGSEA and EnrichR/MSigDB. Transposable element (TE) expression was quantified using STAR alignment and featureCounts with TEtranscripts annotation, followed by DESeq2-based differential analysis and PCA/volcano plots. dsRNA immunoprecipitation was performed using the J2 monoclonal antibody with a Protein A/G magnetic bead system, and precipitated RNA was analyzed by gel electrophoresis. Isolated dsRNA from ΔAgo2 cells was transfected into wild-type LLC cells to assess inflammatory gene induction (Ccl2, Cxcl10). MAVS knockout was introduced into ΔAgo2 cells to probe RIG-I/MDA5 pathway contributions, and TBK1 was pharmacologically inhibited with BX795 to assess convergent innate immune signaling. Flow cytometry on tumors and tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) was performed 10 days post-treatment initiation, using mechanical and enzymatic digestion, Percoll gradient enrichment for T cells, Live/Dead staining, Fc receptor blocking, and surface/intracellular antibody panels acquired on an LSRFortessa instrument. Western blotting confirmed Ago2 and MAVS protein loss in knockout cell lines. A published human NSCLC transcriptomic dataset of ICI-treated patients was analyzed for correlations between Ago2 expression, an Ago2-dependent gene signature, and patient survival.
